input_signals.name: WeakestLinkSolvency
input_signals.expression: MIN(IND_ZSCORE(RATIO(che, lct)), IND_ZSCORE(RATIO(SUB(revt, cogs), at)))
input_signals.hypothesis: Liquidity and operating profitability are not substitutes in avoiding distress: a cash-rich firm with no gross margin eventually burns the cash, and a profitable firm without liquidity can still fail a funding test, so expected returns should be governed by whichever dimension is weakest rather than by their average.
input_signals.reasoning: Taking the minimum of two industry-standardized channels imposes a non-substitutable complementarity that additive composites (Z-score, F-score) and multiplicative products cannot represent, so it is a structurally new interaction rather than a repackaged solvency index. If the minimum outperforms an additive combination of the same two inputs, that is direct evidence the quality-distress interaction is complementary rather than linear.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: min( ind_zscore( ratio( che, lct ) ), ind_zscore( ratio( sub( revt, cogs ), at ) ) )

input_signals.name: TripleWeakestLinkSolvency
input_signals.expression: MIN(IND_ZSCORE(RATIO(che, lct)), MIN(IND_ZSCORE(RATIO(SUB(revt, cogs), at)), IND_ZSCORE(NEG(RATIO(ADD(dltt, dlc), at)))))
input_signals.hypothesis: Survival requires liquidity, operating profitability, and moderate debt simultaneously; a firm's expected return is governed by its single weakest solvency dimension because strength elsewhere cannot substitute for the binding constraint, and the market prices an average rather than a minimum.
input_signals.reasoning: The two-channel minimum already produced the strongest joint evidence in the archive, so the informative next step is whether adding the debt-burden dimension makes the binding constraint sharper or merely adds a stale leverage tilt. All three channels are industry z-scored levels with no rank multiplier, preserving the monotone cross-sectional variation that the Fama-MacBeth slope needs.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: min( ind_zscore( ratio( che, lct ) ), min( ind_zscore( ratio( sub( revt, cogs ), at ) ), ind_zscore( neg( ratio( add( dltt, dlc ), at ) ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: MarginRepairUnderLiquidityStress
input_signals.expression: MUL(RANK(NEG(RATIO(che, lt))), IND_ZSCORE(NEG(DELTA(RATIO(cogs, revt), 1))))
input_signals.hypothesis: For cash-poor firms the direction of unit economics is decisive: a falling cost-of-goods-to-revenue ratio signals that the firm is repairing its operating model before liquidity runs out, while rising unit costs in the same liquidity state signal an approaching funding failure; for cash-rich firms the same margin change is second-order.
input_signals.reasoning: This channel is cost-side dynamics rather than earnings level, volatility, or accruals, so it is not a restatement of any archive signal, and the signed margin-change leg gives a genuine two-sided spread within the liquidity-stressed group. It also stress-tests the rank-times-z structure a second time on a channel where the conditioning variable (margin change) is close to mean-zero, which is where that structure should perform best in Fama-MacBeth.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( rank( neg( ratio( che, lt ) ) ), ind_zscore( neg( delta( ratio( cogs, revt ), 1 ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: GrossProfitCoverageOfNearTermClaims
input_signals.expression: MUL(RANK(NEG(RATIO(pi, at))), IND_ZSCORE(RATIO(SUB(revt, cogs), lct)))
input_signals.hypothesis: Among firms with weak or negative pretax income, the decisive question is whether the still-running operations generate enough gross profit to cover near-term obligations; such firms can refinance and recover, while weak-bottom-line firms whose gross profit is small relative to current liabilities are genuinely insolvent.
input_signals.reasoning: Removing dp eliminates the mechanical anti-correlation the critic identified — the quality leg is no longer an algebraic function of pi, so within loss-makers the ordering cannot collapse into depreciation intensity — and scaling gross profit by current liabilities rather than assets makes the quality leg itself a coverage concept rather than a profitability level. The continuous severity rank keeps the sort populated across the whole cross-section while concentrating weight where the distress mechanism operates.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( rank( neg( ratio( pi, at ) ) ), ind_zscore( ratio( sub( revt, cogs ), lct ) ) )

input_signals.name: RecoveryTrendWithinBindingDistress
input_signals.expression: MUL(RANK(NEG(MIN(IND_ZSCORE(RATIO(che, lct)), IND_ZSCORE(RATIO(SUB(revt, cogs), at))))), IND_ZSCORE(TREND(RATIO(SUB(revt, cogs), at), 5)))
input_signals.hypothesis: The weakest-link score identifies which firms are actually constrained; among those firms, the direction of gross profitability decides whether the constraint is relaxing or tightening, so improving multi-year gross profitability earns large abnormal returns precisely where the binding constraint is tight and deteriorating profitability is punished hardest there.
input_signals.reasoning: This uses the archive winner as a conditioning variable rather than as a predictor, converting a static state measure into a state-times-direction interaction that no single-theme signal can express. The magnitude leg is non-negative (distress intensity) and the sign leg is a centered trend, giving a two-sided spread concentrated in the constrained subsample instead of re-sorting on the level premium already documented.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( rank( neg( min( ind_zscore( ratio( che, lct ) ), ind_zscore( ratio( sub( revt, cogs ), at ) ) ) ) ), ind_zscore( trend( ratio( sub( revt, cogs ), at ), 5 ) ) )

input_signals.name: WorkingCapitalBuildWithMarginDecay
input_signals.expression: MUL(RANK(DELTA(RATIO(wcap, revt), 1)), IND_ZSCORE(NEG(DELTA(RATIO(SUB(revt, cogs), revt), 1))))
input_signals.hypothesis: A ballooning working-capital position relative to revenue means inventory is not selling and receivables are not collecting; that build is benign when margins are holding but signals impending distress when it coincides with margin decay, because the firm is financing unsold output while its unit economics erode.
input_signals.reasoning: This is an operating-cycle deterioration channel that no archive signal touches: the distress dimension is the change in the working-capital stock per unit of revenue, and the quality dimension is the contemporaneous direction of gross margin, so the signal fires only for the toxic combination and reverses sign for firms building working capital while margins expand (a growth, not distress, state). Both legs are changes, so the construct is orthogonal to the level-based composites already tested.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( rank( delta( ratio( wcap, revt ), 1 ) ), ind_zscore( neg( delta( ratio( sub( revt, cogs ), revt ), 1 ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: OwnHistoryLiquidityLowWithIntactMargins
input_signals.expression: MUL(RANK(NEG(TS_RANK(RATIO(che, lct), 5))), IND_ZSCORE(RATIO(SUB(revt, cogs), at)))
input_signals.hypothesis: Distress is partly a within-firm event: a firm sitting at the bottom of its own five-year liquidity range is under transient funding stress, and if its gross profitability is intact that stress is temporary and mean-reverting, whereas the same within-firm liquidity low with weak gross profitability marks structural decline.
input_signals.reasoning: Every archive signal measures distress cross-sectionally, so within-firm liquidity position is a new information axis that automatically neutralizes stable firm- and industry-level differences in optimal cash holdings. The centered gross-profitability leg supplies the sign, so the prediction is explicitly conditional: liquidity depletion is good news for profitable firms and bad news for unprofitable ones.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( rank( neg( ts_rank( ratio( che, lct ), 5 ) ) ), ind_zscore( ratio( sub( revt, cogs ), at ) ) )

input_signals.name: ShortDebtFundingShortfallScaled
input_signals.expression: IND_ZSCORE(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(dlc, ADD(che, SUB(revt, cogs))), at), 1))
input_signals.hypothesis: The economically meaningful distress quantity is the dollar shortfall between debt maturing within the year and the internal funds available to retire it (cash plus a year of gross profit), expressed per unit of assets; firms with a large positive shortfall must refinance on adverse terms and earn low subsequent returns.
input_signals.reasoning: The archive's strongest alpha came from this economic gap but as a quotient whose denominator can be tiny or negative, which is exactly why the Fama-MacBeth slope collapsed to -0.49 while the quintile sort worked; expressing the same shortfall as a numerator over a strictly positive scale preserves both the ordering and the magnitude information a linear slope needs. Industry standardization additionally removes sector differences in normal maturity structure, so the surviving variation is firm-specific refinancing pressure.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: ind_zscore( winsor( ratio( sub( dlc, add( che, sub( revt, cogs ) ) ), at ), 1 ) )

input_signals.name: CapacityAdjustedProfitInWorkingCapitalDeficit
input_signals.expression: MUL(RANK(NEG(RATIO(wcap, at))), IND_ZSCORE(RATIO(SUB(SUB(revt, cogs), dp), at)))
input_signals.hypothesis: A working-capital deficit means the firm must fund its operating cycle from external short-term credit; that is sustainable only if operations earn a surplus after replacing consumed capacity, so profit net of depreciation is the relevant quality measure in exactly this state and firms failing to cover depreciation while running a deficit are contracting toward failure.
input_signals.reasoning: The earlier working-capital-deficit conditioning failed when paired with a volatility leg, but the diagnosis is that second-moment quality channels have been uniformly weak in this archive while level channels have been strong, so pairing the same distress axis with a capacity-adjusted profitability level is a substantive rather than cosmetic change. Subtracting depreciation makes the quality leg a maintainable-surplus measure distinct from the gross profitability used elsewhere, which matters most for asset-heavy firms funding an operating-cycle deficit.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( rank( neg( ratio( wcap, at ) ) ), ind_zscore( ratio( sub( sub( revt, cogs ), dp ), at ) ) )

input_signals.name: MaturityWallAgainstSelfLiquidatingAssets
input_signals.expression: MUL(RANK(RATIO(dlc, at)), IND_ZSCORE(RATIO(cogs, SUB(act, che))))
input_signals.hypothesis: Debt coming due can be met by converting the operating asset base into cash, but only if that base actually turns: a firm whose inventory and receivables are consumed rapidly by operations (high cost of goods relative to non-cash current assets) can liquidate its way through a maturity wall, while a firm holding slow-moving, stale operating assets cannot realize them at anything near book value when it needs to.
input_signals.reasoning: This abandons the minimum family entirely and drops gross profit from both legs, so it cannot be collinear with WeakestLinkSolvency; the conditioning channel is asset-liquidity quality measured by operating turnover of non-cash current assets, a dimension the archive has never used. The maturing-debt rank supplies magnitude and the centered turnover z-score supplies sign, so the prediction is explicitly state-dependent: turnover matters for firms facing a wall and is second-order otherwise.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( rank( ratio( dlc, at ) ), ind_zscore( ratio( cogs, sub( act, che ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: SelfFundingRecordUnderClaimPressure
input_signals.expression: MUL(RANK(RATIO(lct, at)), ZSCORE(TS_COUNT(INDICATOR(SUB(ADD(che, SUB(revt, cogs)), lct), 0), 5)))
input_signals.hypothesis: What protects a firm with heavy near-term claims is a demonstrated history of clearing them from internal resources: the number of the last five years in which cash plus gross profit exceeded current liabilities is a record of self-sufficiency that investors do not extract from the latest balance sheet, and firms with claim pressure but no such record are the ones that eventually fail to roll.
input_signals.reasoning: A threshold-crossing frequency is not a monotone transform of the coverage level — two firms with identical current coverage can differ sharply in how often they actually cleared their obligations — so this is distinct from both WeakestLinkSolvency and DemonstratedCoverageFloor, which use levels and minima respectively. The count is bounded and discrete, which makes the portfolio extremes stable, and the claim-pressure rank restricts the economic content to the population where a funding record matters.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( rank( ratio( lct, at ) ), zscore( ts_count( indicator( sub( add( che, sub( revt, cogs ) ), lct ), 0 ), 5 ) ) )

input_signals.name: ShortfallWithWeakCashCoverage
input_signals.expression: MUL(RANK(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(dlc, ADD(che, SUB(revt, cogs))), at), 1)), IND_ZSCORE(NEG(RATIO(oancf, lct))))
input_signals.hypothesis: A near-term funding shortfall is a timing problem for firms whose operating cash flow comfortably covers current liabilities and an existential problem for firms whose cash flow does not; the shortfall should therefore predict returns only in interaction with realized cash coverage, not uniformly.
input_signals.reasoning: The shortfall state now has the archive's strongest unconditional evidence, so the highest-value question is what sharpens it, and the conditioning channel here is operating cash coverage — a variable outside the shortfall's own construction, which avoids the collinearity that sank earlier gross-profit-on-gross-profit pairings. The non-negative shortfall rank supplies intensity while the centered cash-coverage z-score supplies the sign, so cash-covered firms with a shortfall are predicted to earn positive abnormal returns.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( rank( winsor( ratio( sub( dlc, add( che, sub( revt, cogs ) ) ), at ), 1 ) ), ind_zscore( neg( ratio( oancf, lct ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: ShortfallDeterioration
input_signals.expression: IND_ZSCORE(WINSOR(DELTA(RATIO(SUB(dlc, ADD(che, SUB(revt, cogs))), at), 1), 1))
input_signals.hypothesis: If investors underreact to changes in refinancing pressure rather than mispricing its level, then the year-over-year deterioration in the funding shortfall should carry the predictive content, with firms whose gap widened sharply underperforming regardless of where the level sits.
input_signals.reasoning: State versus event is the one unresolved question about the archive's strongest mechanism, and separating them determines whether the final generations should build on levels or on transitions. The change is taken on an already asset-scaled, winsorized quantity, avoiding the ill-defined growth rates that failed earlier, and if the change effect is weak we can conclude the shortfall is priced as a persistent risk state rather than as news.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: ind_zscore( winsor( delta( ratio( sub( dlc, add( che, sub( revt, cogs ) ) ), at ), 1 ), 1 ) )

input_signals.name: PeakHistoricalFundingShortfall
input_signals.expression: IND_ZSCORE(WINSOR(TS_MAX(RATIO(SUB(dlc, ADD(che, SUB(revt, cogs))), at), 5), 1))
input_signals.hypothesis: Refinancing stress leaves a scar: a firm that has run a large maturing-debt-minus-internal-funds gap at any point in the last five years faces tighter credit terms, shorter maturities and more restrictive covenants even after its current gap closes, so its worst realized shortfall predicts low returns beyond its present balance sheet.
input_signals.reasoning: This is not a smoothing of the champion but a different information object — the maximum over the firm's own recent history rather than its current value — and together with the already-accepted level and one-year-change specifications it decomposes the shortfall state into current pressure, news, and past scarring, which is the decomposition that should guide the final generations. The floor analogue of this idea (worst realized coverage) delivered an independent reliable alpha of +3.5% with t 3.17, so worst-case history carries pricing content that current levels do not.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: ind_zscore( winsor( ts_max( ratio( sub( dlc, add( che, sub( revt, cogs ) ) ), at ), 5 ), 1 ) )

input_signals.name: WorstDangerShortfallOrBrokenProfit
input_signals.expression: MAX(IND_ZSCORE(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(dlc, ADD(che, SUB(revt, cogs))), at), 1)), IND_ZSCORE(NEG(RATIO(SUB(SUB(revt, cogs), dp), at))))
input_signals.hypothesis: A firm is endangered if either of two independent conditions holds — its maturing debt exceeds its internal funds, or its operations fail to earn a surplus after replacing consumed capacity — and neither strength rescues the other, so expected returns are governed by whichever danger is larger.
input_signals.reasoning: The archive shows that a minimum over *safety* channels works (alpha +4.7%, t 4.03) and that multiplying the shortfall by a centered conditioner destroys its alpha, so the correct way to interact the two strongest channels is a worst-of operator on a common danger scale, which preserves each channel's main effect while imposing non-substitutability. The two legs draw on different parts of the firm — the maturity structure and the capacity-adjusted income statement — so this is not a re-scaling of a single quantity.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: max( ind_zscore( winsor( ratio( sub( dlc, add( che, sub( revt, cogs ) ) ), at ), 1 ) ), ind_zscore( neg( ratio( sub( sub( revt, cogs ), dp ), at ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: CumulativeSelfFundingSurplus
input_signals.expression: IND_ZSCORE(WINSOR(TS_SUM(RATIO(SUB(ADD(che, SUB(revt, cogs)), lct), at), 5), 1))
input_signals.hypothesis: Solvency is demonstrated cumulatively: the sum over five years of the scaled surplus of cash plus gross profit over current liabilities measures how consistently a firm has been able to fund its own near-term claims, and firms with a large cumulative surplus are priced as if only the current balance sheet mattered.
input_signals.reasoning: The count-based version of this idea had a strong slope (fmb 3.81) but zero alpha because a 0–5 integer creates massive ties so the sorted extremes were set by the conditioning rank, and replacing the count with a continuous cumulative magnitude removes both the ties and the non-negative conditioner. It is distinct from the floor specification (worst single year) because it rewards the size and duration of the surplus rather than its minimum.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: ind_zscore( winsor( ts_sum( ratio( sub( add( che, sub( revt, cogs ) ), lct ), at ), 5 ), 1 ) )

input_signals.name: WeakestLinkCumulativeCashEarningsVersusClaims
input_signals.expression: MIN(IND_ZSCORE(TS_SUM(RATIO(ADD(pi, dp), at), 5)), IND_ZSCORE(NEG(RATIO(lct, at))))
input_signals.hypothesis: Two things keep a firm out of default: a stock of cash earnings actually accumulated over the cycle, and a claims structure light enough that this accumulation is not immediately consumed. A firm that has generated five years of pre-depreciation earnings has a demonstrated resource base, but that base is irrelevant if near-term claims dwarf it, so the weaker dimension binds.
input_signals.reasoning: Both legs are new to the archive: cumulative five-year pre-depreciation earnings is a flow-accumulation quality measure distinct from the retained-earnings level and from any single-year profitability, and claims intensity replaces the cash-to-current-liabilities conditioner used repeatedly elsewhere, so this shares no inputs with the shortfall family. The worst-of structure preserves each channel's main effect instead of averaging two archive signals, and adding depreciation back makes the quality leg a cash-earning measure rather than an accounting one.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: min( ind_zscore( ts_sum( ratio( add( pi, dp ), at ), 5 ) ), ind_zscore( neg( ratio( lct, at ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: DownsideProfitDangerMax
input_signals.expression: MAX(IND_ZSCORE(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(dlc, ADD(che, SUB(revt, cogs))), at), 1)), IND_ZSCORE(NEG(TS_MIN(RATIO(SUB(SUB(revt, cogs), dp), at), 5))))
input_signals.hypothesis: What makes a funding gap lethal is not average profitability but the firm's demonstrated downside: if its capacity-adjusted profit has fallen to or below zero at some point in the last five years, lenders know the firm can stop covering its own capital consumption, so the worse of current financing pressure and worst-case operating surplus should price distress.
input_signals.reasoning: The floor concept has independently produced reliable alphas in this archive (DemonstratedCoverageFloor +3.5%, t 3.17), and pairing a downside quality leg with the current funding danger asks whether the interaction operates through realized downside rather than the current level — the mirror of the question asked in Signal 2 on the distress side. Together the two signals decompose which side of the interaction carries the historical information.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: max( ind_zscore( winsor( ratio( sub( dlc, add( che, sub( revt, cogs ) ) ), at ), 1 ) ), ind_zscore( neg( ts_min( ratio( sub( sub( revt, cogs ), dp ), at ), 5 ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: AbnormalRefinancingPressure
input_signals.expression: IND_ZSCORE(WINSOR(SUB(RATIO(SUB(dlc, ADD(che, SUB(revt, cogs))), at), MA(RATIO(SUB(dlc, ADD(che, SUB(revt, cogs))), at), 5)), 1))
input_signals.hypothesis: Firms differ permanently in how much short-term funding their business model requires, so what signals trouble is refinancing pressure above the firm's own normal level; a distributor that always runs a gap is not distressed, whereas a firm whose gap has moved well above its own five-year norm is.
input_signals.reasoning: This changes the normalization axis rather than the horizon: the cross-sectional level, its one-year change, and its five-year peak have all been tested, but never the deviation from the firm's own recent norm, and the within-firm axis produced the archive's strongest slope elsewhere (fmb 4.87). It should also fix the specific failure of the one-year change specification, which had a powerful slope but no alpha because single-year swings reverse, whereas a deviation from a five-year mean is a persistent state.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: ind_zscore( winsor( sub( ratio( sub( dlc, add( che, sub( revt, cogs ) ) ), at ), ma( ratio( sub( dlc, add( che, sub( revt, cogs ) ) ), at ), 5 ) ), 1 ) )

input_signals.name: StockVersusFlowSolvencyWeakestLink
input_signals.expression: MIN(IND_ZSCORE(WINSOR(TS_SUM(RATIO(SUB(ADD(che, SUB(revt, cogs)), lct), at), 5), 1)), IND_ZSCORE(RATIO(SUB(SUB(revt, cogs), dp), at)))
input_signals.hypothesis: Solvency requires both an accumulated record of having funded its own claims over the cycle and current earning power after replacing consumed capacity; a firm with a strong five-year record but no current surplus is in decline, and one with a good current surplus but no accumulated record has never been tested, so the weaker of the two binds.
input_signals.reasoning: Unlike swapping a highly correlated leg into the incumbent minimum, this pairs channels at genuinely different horizons — a five-year cumulative resource stock and a current-year capacity-adjusted flow — each of which delivered independently reliable alphas (+3.7% t 3.32 and +2.6% t 3.00) from different information. The horizon complementarity is the economic claim being tested: demonstrated history and current earning power are not substitutes for survival.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: min( ind_zscore( winsor( ts_sum( ratio( sub( add( che, sub( revt, cogs ) ), lct ), at ), 5 ), 1 ) ), ind_zscore( ratio( sub( sub( revt, cogs ), dp ), at ) ) )

input_signals.name: FundingProfitAndTradeCreditDanger
input_signals.expression: MAX(IND_ZSCORE(NEG(RATIO(SUB(SUB(revt, cogs), dp), at))), MAX(IND_ZSCORE(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(dlc, ADD(che, SUB(revt, cogs))), at), 1)), IND_ZSCORE(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(SUB(lct, dlc), che), cogs), 1))))
input_signals.hypothesis: Insolvency can arrive through maturing debt, through withdrawn supplier terms, or through operations that fail to cover the cost of replacing consumed capacity; because none of these is neutralized by strength on the others, the largest of the three dangers should price expected returns.
input_signals.reasoning: The earlier three-leg experiment diluted because its added leg was a stale leverage ratio, whereas all three legs here have delivered independent, reliably signed alphas of roughly -4% or better from different parts of the financial statements. Comparing it against the two-leg version in Signal 1 identifies whether the operating-surplus danger contains information beyond the two financing dangers, which is the central quality-versus-distress question of this project.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: max( ind_zscore( neg( ratio( sub( sub( revt, cogs ), dp ), at ) ) ), max( ind_zscore( winsor( ratio( sub( dlc, add( che, sub( revt, cogs ) ) ), at ), 1 ) ), ind_zscore( winsor( ratio( sub( sub( lct, dlc ), che ), cogs ), 1 ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: MaturityMismatchOrBrokenProfitDanger
input_signals.expression: MAX(IND_ZSCORE(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(dlc, che), dp), 1)), IND_ZSCORE(NEG(RATIO(SUB(SUB(revt, cogs), dp), at))))
input_signals.hypothesis: The danger from short-term funding is best measured against the life of the assets it finances rather than against annual internal funds: firms whose net short-term debt equals many years of capital consumption are financing long-lived capacity with on-demand money, and that exposure is lethal when operations cannot cover capacity replacement.
input_signals.reasoning: The asset-life mismatch channel produced an alpha of -4.5% with a null slope on its own, so pairing it with the profitability danger inside the bounded worst-of structure tests both whether mismatch is a better distress leg than the internal-funds shortfall and whether the operator repairs its slope. Because the mismatch leg contains no profit term, the two legs here are less collinear than in any previous danger pairing.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: max( ind_zscore( winsor( ratio( sub( dlc, che ), dp ), 1 ) ), ind_zscore( neg( ratio( sub( sub( revt, cogs ), dp ), at ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: TradeCreditSafetyWithGrossProfit
input_signals.expression: MIN(IND_ZSCORE(RATIO(SUB(revt, cogs), at)), IND_ZSCORE(NEG(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(SUB(lct, dlc), che), cogs), 1))))
input_signals.hypothesis: A firm is safe only if it both earns a substantial gross return on assets and does not depend on suppliers to finance its operating cycle; profitable firms leaning heavily on trade credit are one supplier decision from a liquidity event, and conservatively financed firms without profitability erode anyway.
input_signals.reasoning: This replaces the cash-to-current-liabilities leg of the archive's best long-side signal — which is essentially the published cash-holdings effect — with a genuinely new liability-structure leg that has independent portfolio evidence, so it is a new pairing rather than a correlated leg swap. It also provides the long-side counterpart to this batch's danger composites, letting us see whether the trade-credit channel works symmetrically in safety and danger form.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: min( ind_zscore( ratio( sub( revt, cogs ), at ) ), ind_zscore( neg( winsor( ratio( sub( sub( lct, dlc ), che ), cogs ), 1 ) ) ) )
